question: What trailing space/tab patterns survive in strictly parsed clear-signed bodies in the preserved 133-path G-02 archive, after exact and canonical deduplication?
rules: No stripping leading indentation or normalizing raw bytes before parsing.
Exact line armor only; require Hash headers and blank separator; exclude signature armor and opaque PGP MESSAGE packets.
Count every body line including empty and whitespace-only lines; expose suffix spaces/tabs and line endings.

Exact body identity includes raw line terminators; canonical identity dash-unescapes, strips trailing space/tab, then joins with LF; this is a comparison key, not a complete OpenPGP verification implementation.
Match only entire or prefix nonzero-count sequences against the three literal source lists; no binary decoding, adaptive thresholds, broad cipher search or LP2 inference.
Saved G-02 verdicts provide context; a valid cleartext signature ignores trailing whitespace and cannot authenticate its originality.
Run planted parser fixtures before census; independently recompute line counts and dedup after census.
Optional isolated GPG control uses only archived public key and a saved PASS message, modifies trailing whitespace, and records validity.
